subject: Clarify data ownership, breach notice timing, and next steps
messages:
From: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@medicore.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-01T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up from demo — DPA clarifications

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo earlier — the team found the latency/cost controls compelling. Before we proceed to procurement, Legal asked for a couple of clarifications on the DPA and how Redwood treats customer data for our clinical pilot. Can you confirm the following?

1) Controller vs. Processor: We need explicit language that MedicoRe (us) is the controller and Redwood is a processor for telemetry and inference logs. Will Redwood accept a controller/processor mapping clause that reflects that?

2) Subprocessors: Can you provide the current subprocessors list and clarify the notification window if you add a new subprocessor that will process PII? Our policy requires 30 days notice.

3) Breach notification timing: Per our contracts, we must be notified of any suspected data breach affecting customer data within 72 hours. What is Redwood's SLA and practical turnaround for notifying customers and providing an initial incident summary?

4) Data residency & retention: For the pilot we need logs retained for 180 days in us-west region and any exported audit logs to be under our KMS. Is that supported?

If it's easier, send a marked-up DPA or short FAQ for Legal. Attaching our procurement checklist separately.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call this week if helpful.

—Anna
Anna Lopez
Director, Platform Integrations
MediCore Health
anna.lopez@medicore.com
(415) 555-0198

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@medicore.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-01T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — DPA clarifications

Hi Anna — great to hear the demo resonated. Thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below and I attached a redline of our standard DPA (Redwood_DPA_v2_redlines.pdf) plus a short logging matrix (system-logging-matrix.xlsx) for your ops/legal review.

Quick answers:
- Controller/Processor: Yes — Redwood accepts controller=customer / processor=Redwood mapping. In our DPA we include specific language to that effect and a section on obligations for each party. If MedicoRe needs controller-specific indemnities, loop in your counsel and we can discuss.
- Subprocessors: We maintain an up-to-date list; we provide 30 days notice for major subprocessors and 14 days for non-production tooling by default. We can agree to 30 days notice for subprocessors that will process PII (we'll mark that as a negotiated term in the redline).
- Breach notice: Our standard commitment is notification within 48 hours of Redwood confirming a breach that impacts customer data, and an initial incident summary within 72 hours. For high-risk PII exposures we can include a clause committing to 48-hour initial notice and a detailed remediation plan within 7 business days.
- Residency & retention: We support region-scoped deployments in us-west and can hold logs for 180 days; we also support customer-managed KMS for exported logs and artifacts in Dedicated / Private deployments. For Hosted we provide tenant-level encryption and can discuss Bring-Your-Own-KMS on a case-by-case for pilots.

Next steps I propose:
1) Legal & Security: I'll send this thread to our security and legal leads (cc'd Kimberly) and ask them to review the two attachments and propose any targeted language changes.
2) If your legal team wants language changes, please mark up the DPA and return; we'll aim for a 3-business-day turnaround for an initial response.
3) I'll schedule a 30-minute pick-up call with your legal and security to walk through the redline if helpful.

Would Thursday 10:00–10:30 PT work for a short review call?

Thanks,
Rachel

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-03T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up from demo — DPA clarifications

Rachel — thanks for the context and for attaching the redline. Short answers and proposed language below; attaching the current subprocessors export for MediCore review.

1) Controller/Processor: Confirmed — Redwood will accept language that MedicoRe is controller and Redwood is processor. Proposed clause (for DPA redline): 
"For the performance of the Services, the parties agree that Customer is the data controller and Redwood Inference, Inc. is the data processor with respect to Customer Data. Redwood shall process Customer Data only on documented instructions from Customer, except as required by law."

2) Subprocessors & notice: Current subprocessors list attached (subprocessors-current-20271203.csv). Standard notice: 30 days for subprocessors that process production customer PII; 14 days for non-production/tooling. Proposed redline: commit to 30 days notice and right to object.

3) Breach notification timing: We can commit to initial notification within 48 hours of Redwood confirming unauthorized access materially affecting Customer Data, and an initial incident summary within 72 hours. Proposed clause: 
"Redwood will notify Customer of any confirmed or reasonably suspected security incident affecting Customer Data within 48 hours of confirmation and will provide an initial incident report within 72 hours, followed by regular updates. For incidents involving PII with material risk to data subjects, Redwood will prioritize escalation and provide a remediation plan within 7 business days."

4) Residency & retention / BYO-KMS: We support retention for 180 days in the us-west region. BYO-KMS for exported audit logs is available for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted pilots we can provide tenant-scoped encryption with provider-managed keys; we can offer a migration path to Dedicated pilot with BYO-KMS if MediCore requires KMS control for the pilot.

Next steps I recommend we: 1) return the redlined DPA with the commented clauses above (I highlighted them in the attached redline), 2) provide the subprocessors CSV and the system logging matrix, and 3) offer a 30-minute legal/security review call (I can join if needed).

I'll attach: subprocessors-current-20271203.csv and a short note file with proposed redline snippets. Let me know if you want me to push the final redline to them directly or route through Rachel.

—Sergio
